messages:
mira: Heads-up — Kale Labs (kale@kalelabs.com) on a trial just finished the SSO onboarding flow but reports there is no API key in their Console. They tried a sample request and got `401: Invalid API key`. Customer is on a short call, asking for a quick triage. :rotating_light:

jordan: I created ticket CS-5123 and pinged CSM. Quick check: in the admin UI the org exists (org_id=org_78a9) and user shows as active, but under Projects -> Keys there's nothing. Tried the admin API: `GET /v1/projects/org_78a9/keys` -> 404. No keys.

ticketbot: Ticket CS-5123 created and assigned to support; priority: P2 (trial customer). Linked to internal SR-2987.

mira: Repro steps from customer (shared):
1) SSO via Okta (saml) -> accepted
2) selected org name "Kale Labs"
3) accepted terms -> landed on /console/projects
4) clicked "Get API Key" -> spinner, then nothing. No error in UI.

kale-support: We also tried `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer " "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health"` and got `401`. We haven't used a key yet, so not sure if action needed from our side.

samir: Can you paste the provisioning job logs for the onboarding run? I want the request_id from the onboarding-worker. Likely a job failed silently. Common causes: missing default project row, or a FK constraint when creating api_key.

jordan: Pasting the onboarding-worker tail (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] INFO onboarding.worker request_id=rid_9f1 provisioning-start org=org_78a9 user=kale@kalelabs.com
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] INFO onboarding.worker request_id=rid_9f1 create-default-project -> attempt insert project(org_78a9_default)
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] ERROR onboarding.worker request_id=rid_9f1 create-default-project -> insert failed: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "projects_name_key"
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] INFO onboarding.worker request_id=rid_9f1 lookup-project by name org_78a9_default -> not found
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] ERROR onboarding.worker request_id=rid_9f1 provision-api-key -> abort: missing project row
```

samir: That error is interesting — duplicate key on insert followed by lookup-not-found suggests a race or a half-committed transaction that was rolled back but left the unique index reserved (or a different row with similar normalized name exists). Could also be a normalization mismatch between SSO org slug and DB project name.

mira: I searched Projects table and I see a project with name `kale-labs` (hyphen) and org_id `org_78a9`, but the onboarding worker attempts to create `org_78a9_default` (underscore + org id). The two naming schemes don't match.

samir: Aha. Hypothesis: SSO path creates a project earlier with normalized name `kale-labs` and the onboarding-worker later tries to create `org_78a9_default`, hits unique constraint because of our normalization function (both normalize to same slug), then fails to find the project because the lookup uses the other name key. So downstream code aborts without creating API key.

rebecca: I'll run a targeted backfill to create missing api keys for any orgs with users but no keys. Plan: run internal endpoint `POST /internal/backfill/provision-keys` with filter `org_id=org_78a9`. Before that I want to verify we won't double-create keys. Samir, can you confirm idempotency?

samir: Backfill endpoint is idempotent if called with `dry_run=false` and `force=false`. It uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` for keys. I'll instrument a quick additional check to avoid creating a second default project. Also will add a guard to normalize names consistently.

jordan: Customer update: I created a temporary support key (read-only, expires in 72h) and sent it to them so they can continue testing. Marked it `support-temp:kale_org_78a9`. Kale confirmed they can now call the API and see basic responses.

kale-support: Thanks, that works for now. We prefer a permanent fix though — please keep us posted.

samir: Short-term mitigation: run the backfill for org_78a9 now and monitor logs. Medium-term fix: patch normalization in onboarding-worker and add a retry on unique constraint where lookup should reconcile. Long-term: add unit test for mixed normalization paths plus an end-to-end SSO onboarding test. I'll open SR-2987 with these action items.

rebecca: Executed backfill at 09:45 UTC against org_78a9. Logs show provisioning job created 1 key: `key_prod_kale_01` and wrote to keys table. Post-check: `GET /v1/projects/org_78a9/keys` now returns the new key. Notifying CSM and marking CS-5123 as "provisioned (manual)".

mira: Customer notified and verified. They asked whether billing will be affected — I told them the temporary key is limited and we won't bill while they're on trial; permanent key will be created as part of backfill and normal billing applies after they enable paid usage. CSM confirmed.

samir: I'll push the patch to onboarding-worker normalization and add a short migration to reconcile existing projects with mixed slugs. Target deploy window: today 18:00 UTC. I'll add a post-deploy smoke test that runs the same onboarding flow with an Okta test org.

ticketbot: CS-5123 -> SR-2987 updated: status=investigating, owner=samir, eta=2026-03-14T18:00:00Z.

mira: Closing loop for now. If anyone sees other SSO trial signups failing, please add them to SR-2987. :lock:
